Start IronAFS: licence, decisions, workflow and scaffold

IronAFS is a modern AFS client in Rust, meant to work with existing AFS
cells through one shared core and thin per-OS layers (macOS FSKit,
Windows Cloud Files, Linux FUSE), with no kernel extensions of its own.
This first commit holds no client code yet. It sets out how the project
is licensed, decided, built and reviewed:

- Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later for all of IronAFS's own material, with
  REUSE-compliant SPDX headers, and DCO sign-offs for contributions.
- ADR 0001: the licence, and the don't-copy rule: no code from OpenAFS,
  AuriStor or the Linux kernel's AFS and Rx implementations; IronAFS is
  written from published specifications and observed behaviour.
- ADR 0002: how AI models are used, how commits credit them, and how
  the work is done in the open.
- The workflow (change classes E/I/P/S/R and their review seats), the
  coding standards, the dependency policy, and the research the
  decisions rest on.
- A Cargo workspace with a placeholder `afs` binary, pinned toolchain,
  clippy, nextest and cargo-deny configuration, GitHub issue forms,
  Dependabot and CODEOWNERS.

The tree was reviewed in seventeen rounds by models from five families
(GPT, GLM, Gemini, DeepSeek and Claude); every finding and its
disposition is in docs/reviews/2026-11-18-first-public-tree.md and in
each ADR's Review section. The final full-tree review (GPT, round 14)
and the verifications of every change made since (GLM, rounds 15 to
17) found nothing left open.

Class: R
